Thanks again for your time today — really appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Scope: Evaluate Redwood for secure inference for Orchard Health patient-facing and clinician-facing workflows (priority: patient triage assistant).
- Key risks called out: PHI handling, audit logging, and environment isolation for production data.
- Decision timeline: target procurement/contract decision by end of Q1 2027.

Action items / asks: 
1) Please confirm the primary security contact and procurement/legal point-of-contact (name, role, email) — we want to loop the right reviewers for the questionnaire.
2) Share high-level systems expected to be in-scope (e.g., EHR integration, analytics DB, SFTP intake).
3) I attached our standard security overview and the intake questionnaire (we'll tailor after your answers). If you can return the questionnaire within 7 business days, we can scope the review and schedule the kickoff review.

Proposed next meeting: Security kickoff (30–45m) the week of Dec 13 — will include security, engineering, and procurement. If that works, I can send a Doodle or propose 2 slots.

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Overview.pdf (pdf) — high-level controls and SOC2 posture

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

Date: 2026-12-07T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Security review kickoff — intake questionnaire + proposed scope checklist

Tom / Lena — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attaching the intake worksheet (Orchard_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx) — this is purposely short and focuses on the items our security team needs to scope a deeper review. To help us triage, could you confirm the items below when you return the spreadsheet?

1) Systems in scope (production vs. staging) — list hostnames/roles where possible.
2) Data types (PHI, PII, telemetry) and whether data is encrypted at rest/in transit.
3) Integration points (Epic API endpoints, Snowflake schemas, SFTP host) and expected volumes (qps / files per day).
4) Required compliance evidence (SOC 2 report, penetration test reports, BAAs).
5) Timeline constraints — target dates for review completion and any hard procurement deadlines.

Attachments included: 
- Orchard_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx (xlsx) — intake worksheet for your security team
- Redwood_Security_Overview.pdf (pdf) — our controls summary + SOC2 attestation path

Proposed plan after intake: Redwood security & engineering will ingest the worksheet, schedule a 45m technical kickoff with Tom and our security engineer (Neha will join), then produce a scoping doc and list of evidence requests. Expect initial scoping ~3–5 business days after we receive the intake.

Please let me know if you prefer a single combined kickoff (procurement + security) or two separate sessions — I'm happy to coordinate.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks, attaching the preliminary systems list and a network diagram. High level notes here to help guide the intake: 

Systems in scope (production):
- API gateway (east-prod-gw01.orchard.internal) — handles Epic token exchange, TLS termination
- EHR integration (Epic sandboxes + prod endpoints) — data pulled via secure API; contains PHI
- Snowflake (orchard_analytics) — only aggregated telemetry; no PHI at rest in the analytics schema
- SFTP ingestion (sftp.orchard.health) — nightly batch patient lists (PHI) 
- Internal staging cluster (staging-models) — used for model validation; contains de-identified test records

Data flows: PHI enters via SFTP and Epic APIs, tokens are exchanged at the API gateway, payloads forwarded to Redwood inference endpoints. We can provide a redacted sequence diagram.

Evidence: we will need SOC2 Type II, pen test summaries, and BAA for PHI handling in contract. Procurement timeline: aim for signed SOW by end of Q1 2027.

Attachments: Network_Diagram.png (png) — redacted network flow
